successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: 'The Arvernian territory was attached to Aquitania, which now reached as far as the Loire'; 'the civitas of the Arverni, kept within the limits it had held in the period of independence'

ledger.x: c. 250 BC: the Arverni are established in the Massif Central. The page gives no founding date: they 'first appear in the written record at the end of the 3rd century BC' (207 BC, treating with Hasdrubal) after an entity had 'formed for several generations'; the oppidum of Gandaillat is occupied from the first half of…

ledger.cp: Vellavii, Gabali, Cadurci and Eleuteti (Arvernian clients)

ledger.x: 121 BC: Rome meets the Arverni and Allobroges in the Rhône valley.
August 121 BC: Bituitus is crushed at the Isère.
52 BC: Vercingetorix, an Arvernian, leads the Gallic revolt and 'won a victory over the Roman army at Gergovia, the chief oppidum of the Arverni'.
52 BC: 'Vercingetorix was defeated by the Romans at the Battle of Alesia, after which the Arverni lost their power of suzerainty.'
ledger.cp: Vellavii, Gabali, Cadurci and Eleuteti (Arvernian clients)

ledger.x: September 52 BC: Alesia ends the revolt.
52 BC: the Arverni are brought under Rome.
September 52 BC: the independent Arverni end with the surrender of Vercingetorix; the civitas lives on inside Roman Gaul.

wars.name: First Transalpine War
wars.outcome: Roman victory under Domitius Ahenobarbus and Fabius Maximus: Bituitus captured, the Allobroges brought under Roman rule, the province of Gallia Narbonensis established; the Arverni 'retained independence after the war' but lost their dominance.

wars.name: Revolt of Vercingetorix (Gallic Wars, 52 BC)
wars.outcome: Gallic victory at Gergovia, then defeat and surrender at Alesia in September 52; the Arverni lost their suzerainty but kept civitas libera status.

certainty.note: No boundary is given by any page; the territory is the later Auvergne (the Barrington Atlas places the Arverni 'east of the Lemovices and Petrocorii, south of the Bituriges Cubi and Aedui, north of the Ruteni, Cadurci and Vellavii, and…
